primitives.name: Hot Hand Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The so called "hot hand" phenomenon (phrase coined by American basketball fans) refers to the commonly held belief amongst sports fans, coaches and players that sports players can, on occasion, produce sequences of consistently superior (compared to their normal) performance.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes performance can be decomposed into independent trials with constant probability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when trials exhibit autocorrelation or time-varying skill.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian sequential probability update - tracks posterior belief p(skill|data) after observing streaks.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior probability of elevated skill given observed streak length and baseline accuracy.

primitives.name: Momentum Chart Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: A momentum chart was used to identify potentially streaky performance and this data was then compared with the non-streaky data using the chi square test of independence.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes streaky periods are temporally separable from non-streaky periods.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when streakiness is persistent across the entire dataset without clear separation.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction intervals - identifies regions where empirical distribution deviates significantly from IID baseline.
layer2.telemetry: Width of conformal interval at each time point relative to nominal coverage.

primitives.name: Streaky Performance Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore this approach allows streaky performance to contain a few non-successful performances.
primitives.assumptions: Allows for Bernoulli trials with time-varying success probability that clusters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if non-streaky periods also exhibit clustering due to external factors.

layer2.mapping: Hidden Markov Model - two latent states (hot/cold) with different emission probabilities for success/failure.
layer2.telemetry: Likelihood ratio of being in the hot state versus cold state given current observation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is distinguishing true autocorrelation (skill-based streakiness) from apparent streakiness caused by baseline variability. Hot hand detection fails when trials are not independent, leading to inflated false positive rates. Momentum charts provide descriptive summaries but lack formal uncertainty quantification. Streaky models must incorporate temporal dynamics; otherwise they collapse to simple binomial tests. All three primitives rely on ergodicity assumptions that break down in persistent systems. Effective state estimation requires filtering techniques that track changing skill windows.
